Visual judge.toml:99 repeats that mobile usability ownership. Criterion weights are attached to named outcomes; shared setup is not a second weighted criterion. No concrete weight inflation from duplicated ownership was established for this row.

Counterexample attempts: a conforming implementation using native controls, a plain readable monospaced editor, conventional spacing and stacked/tabs/drawer mobile panes is allowed full credit by polish/judge.toml responsive_layout and visual/judge.toml:25,40,55,70,85,99-100; no branded design or particular visual richness is required. For a broken stylish shell, both gates demand actual newly authored execution and shared saved-record retrieval (gates/render/judge.toml cw_workspace_runs_authored_marker; gates/constraints/judge.toml cw_saved_source_shared_across_clean_contexts). Thus there is an intentional low-floor discontinuity: a minimally above-floor app can obtain 0.4303 with perfect presentation. This is an exact analytical/synthetic reducer result under the mandatory policy, not a measured weak-app grade or a confirmed defect in weight allocation. There was no weight-based false failure of the conforming alternative or concrete false pass of a dead shell.
